recognize_zh: 在正常成熟中的骨髓細胞背景裡，中央有一顆特別巨大的細胞，細胞質深藍、豐富，核圓而偏位、染色質較細，體積遠大於周圍骨髓細胞，這是多發性骨髓瘤中的大型（不成熟）漿細胞。
features: Single very large cell, several times the size of surrounding myelocytes
Round, slightly eccentric nucleus with relatively fine chromatin; nucleolus not clearly visible
Abundant, deeply basophilic cytoplasm with irregular borders and faint paranuclear pale zone
Background of normal trilineage maturation: neutrophil precursors, band forms, erythroid precursors, eosinophils
Large fat vacuole adjacent to the cell
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a background of maturing granulocytic and erythroid precursors with a single conspicuous very large cell. This cell has abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm, a round, slightly eccentric nucleus with relatively fine chromatin, and a vague paranuclear clearing, consistent with a large atypical (immature) plasma cell. A single cell is insufficient for diagnosis; the plasma cell percentage, clonality by flow cytometry or kappa/lambda staining, and correlation with serum/urine M-protein are required. Findings are compatible with plasma cell myeloma with large atypical plasma cells in the appropriate context.

ddx.vs: Osteoblasts occur in clusters, have an eccentric nucleus with a hof located away from the nucleus, and are CD138-negative/CD56-variable without light chain restriction.
Immature megakaryocytes show cytoplasmic blebs, a higher N:C ratio and are CD61/CD42b positive rather than CD138 positive.
Carcinoma cells form cohesive clusters with vacuolated cytoplasm and are cytokeratin positive, lacking plasma cell features.
Plasmablastic lymphoma presents as sheets of immunoblastic cells, often EBER positive in HIV patients, without the osteolytic/M-protein myeloma context.
